thread:
cheng: heads-up — saw a 7-12% p50 regression on canary for the 13B packed-attn config after the recent fusion patch. Not obvious from perf counters, but L2 misses spiked on the paged-KV path.

aisha: ouch. can you paste the exact config / flags you used on canary?

cheng: sure — rollout used the usual canary job with these runtime toggles:
```
epilogue_fusion: true
qkv_pack_mode: packed
bias_rope_inplace: true
paged_kv_enable: true
kernel_chooser: auto
```
Microbench (single-GPU synthetic, batch=8): baseline p50=18.2ms, canary p50=20.4ms. tail also worse.

mike: hmm looks like epilogue fusion assumes contiguous KV write pattern. paged_kv makes KV writes scatter-ish which can blow up L2 streaming. Any profiler flamegraphs?

cheng: attached quick nvprof snapshot (summary pasted):
- increased L2 evictions on attention_epilogue_kernel
- higher global_mem_load latency on paged_kv path
- instruction throughput roughly same
So not compute bound, more memory layout churn.

anya: this matches what I saw in a local repro — when paged_kv is enabled we chunk KV into N pages and epilogue was doing a fused write that touches final KV pages out of order. That causes conflict in the L2 set usage. Quick test: disabling bias/rope fusion reduces regression from 10% -> 2%.

mike: can you try disabling only epilogue fusion (keep qkv_pack)? if that fixes perf we can add a chooser heuristic to turn off epilogue when paged_kv is in use. Also check fp32 vs qint8 path — quantized kernels may stress caches differently.

cheng: ran three variants on same canary node:
- baseline (no fusion): 18.2ms
- full fusion: 20.4ms
- full fusion + paged_kv disabled: 18.6ms
- epilogue_fusion=false (qkv & bias/rope still fused): 18.8ms
So epilogue fusion + paged_kv is the culprit.

tim: pragmatic plan: (1) add a short-circuit in kernel chooser to prefer unfused-epilogue when paged_kv_enable && seq_len > 1024 (or when observed page count > X), (2) file a follow-up to rework epilogue write ordering to be page-friendly, (3) run numeric/regression tests for bias/rope fusion change.

cheng: I can flip the chooser in canary now and roll out. Will also open an issue for the epilogue rewrite.

deploy-bot: canary rollout triggered by cheng (2147000018). target: 10% of fleet.

aisha: ping eng-sre in case we need fast rollback. Also add a short note to the release channel so infra knows this is a perf tweak.

cheng: update: chooser flip deployed to canary (epilogue_fusion disabled when paged_kv_enable=true). After flip p50 back to 18.4ms, tail largely normalized. Reverting full fusion on the canary nodes for now.

mike: nice. I'll open a draft PR with a change to the epilogue memory write ordering that should reduce set-conflicts; includes a microbench harness that simulates paged KV layouts. PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/attn-kernels/pulls/1256 (draft).

anya: pls also add a unit test that runs the numeric checks for bias+rope when we toggle fusion flags — we saw tiny FP drift in earlier patches.

cheng: will do. created follow-up ticket RW-4237: "epilogue: page-friendly write ordering + chooser heuristic" and added the microbench numbers + nvprof snapshot.

mike: bonus idea — we could make epilogue fusion respectful of a "write_stride" hint from the paged-kv allocator and emit scatter-safe kernels. Might keep perf wins for contiguous paths while avoiding thrash on paged.

cheng: agreed, adding to RW-4237. thanks all. :thumbsup:
